t.2.77.1: Then, having risen at daybreak and mounted the finest of chariots, Bharata set out swiftly, longing to see Rāma.
t.2.77.2: All the ministers and priests went on ahead of him, having mounted chariots yoked with horses, chariots like the chariot of the sun.
t.2.77.3: Nine thousand elephants, equipped according to rule, followed Bharata, the joy of the Ikṣvāku race, as he went forth.
t.2.77.4: Sixty thousand chariots, bowmen bearing weapons of many kinds, followed Bharata, the illustrious prince, as he went forth.
t.2.77.5: A hundred thousand riders mounted on horses followed Bharata, the glorious prince of the Rāghava line, as he went.
t.2.77.6: Kaikeyī and Sumitrā and the illustrious Kausalyā, rejoicing at the prospect of bringing Rāma back, set out in a resplendent carriage.
t.2.77.7: And throngs of noble men set out to see Rāma together with Lakṣmaṇa, their hearts rejoicing, telling wondrous tales of him alone as they went.
t.2.77.8: When shall we see Rāma, dark as a rain-cloud, mighty-armed, steadfast in spirit and firm in his vows, the dispeller of the world's sorrow?
t.2.77.9: For Rāghava, the moment he is seen, will dispel our grief, just as the rising sun dispels the darkness of the whole world.
t.2.77.10: Thus speaking such auspicious words, the townsfolk, overjoyed and embracing one another, then went their way.
t.2.77.11: And all the others there who were held in esteem, and the merchants as well, all the subjects then set out joyfully toward Rāma.
t.2.77.12: Whatever jewelers there were, and the skilled potters, the weavers, and those who make their living by arms,
t.2.77.13: Workers in peacock feathers, sawyers, ornament-makers and borers of gems, ivory carvers, plasterers, and likewise those who lived by selling perfumes.
t.2.77.15: Washermen and tailors, the headmen of villages and cowherd settlements, actors together with their women, and fishermen likewise, all go forth.
t.2.77.14: Renowned goldsmiths, and likewise washers of woollen blankets, bath attendants and dressers, physicians, incense-makers, and liquor-sellers as well.
t.2.77.16: Brāhmaṇas by the thousands, composed in mind, versed in the Vedas and esteemed for their conduct, followed Bharata on ox-carts as he went.
t.2.77.17: Well attired, in clean garments, their bodies smeared with copper-red unguents, they all slowly followed Bharata in carriages of various kinds.
t.2.77.18: Thrilled and joyful, that army followed the son of Kaikayī; that army, following Bharata, took up its position.
t.2.77.19: Having looked upon the army that had followed him and upon that Gaṅgā of auspicious waters, Bharata, skilled in speech, addressed all his ministers.
t.2.77.20: Encamp my army throughout, just as I wish; having rested now, we shall cross the great river tomorrow.
t.2.77.21: And first I wish to descend into the river and offer water to the king who has gone to heaven, for the sake of the funeral rites.
t.2.77.22: As he spoke thus, the ministers, attentive, said “So be it,” and settled them each separately, according to each one's own wish.
t.2.77.23: Having stationed along that great river Gaṅgā his army, resplendent with its trappings and arrayed in due order, Bharata then encamped there, pondering how to bring back the great-souled Rāma.
